## Purpose and research context

This notebook establishes the descriptive context for the FMD project **before** model training. It measures annual coverage, outcome and predictor nonresponse, the distribution of BRFSS survey weights, and reported **frequent mental distress (FMD)** among American Indian and Alaska Native (AI/AN)-alone adults and other identified single-race adults.

**Outcome:** `FMD = 1` means 14 or more self-reported mentally unhealthy days during the preceding 30 days; `FMD = 0` means fewer than 14 days. Unknown or refused outcomes are excluded from the prevalence numerator and denominator, but retained in the audit.

**Outputs:** two visible charts—annual prevalence with 95% confidence intervals and the annual AI/AN-minus-comparison difference with 95% confidence intervals—plus their supporting tables. This is **not** a prediction model, causal analysis, or longitudinal follow-up of the same individuals. The separate 2025 file is not used.

**Important prerequisite:** Verify from the original BRFSS import/recoding script that `RAW_WEIGHT` is the unchanged CDC `_LLCPWT` weight, `STRAT` is `_STSTR`, and `PSU` corresponds to `_PSU`. A plausible audit does *not* establish these mappings. The survey intervals below are conditional on that verification and on the exclusions used to construct the processed dataset.

## 1. Load existing project helpers and attach the run

This cell finds the RStudio project and loads your existing helper and graph-palette modules. When called from the master notebook, it **uses the current run increment**; when knitted independently, it **allocates a new increment** so no previous artifacts are overwritten.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
# Find the existing RStudio project root without hard-coded local paths.
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)

    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) {
            return(current)
        }

        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(parent, current)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio before running this notebook.")
        }

        current <- parent
    }
}

project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)

# Evaluate the shared R Markdown modules, preserving your current project setup.
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    lines <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(lines, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(lines) == "```")

    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Missing executable chunk or closing fence in ", path)
        }

        paste(lines[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })

    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}

load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")

# The survey package is required for design-aware uncertainty estimates.
check_packages(c("data.table", "ggplot2", "scales", "survey"))

# Keep the master-notebook increment; allocate a new one for standalone knitting.
if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv("ATG_RUN_ID", unset = ""))) {
    start_new_run()
}

run_context <- attach_run()
cat("[RUN] Audit increment:", run_context$id, "\n")
```

## 2. Load the historical dataset and audit respondent coverage

This cell measures how many respondents are available each year, how many have a usable mental-health outcome, whether their original annual weights are positive and finite, and how many states are represented. The audit takes place **before** excluding records with unknown FMD or race.

```{r yearly-coverage}
# Read the pooled 2014–2024 dataset without modifying the saved source file.
historical <- read_historical()
historical[, cohort := race_group(AIAN_ALONE)]

# Tabulate survey availability by year.
annual_audit <- historical[
    ,
    .(
        respondents = .N,
        valid_fmd = sum(valid_outcome(FMD)),
        missing_fmd = sum(!valid_outcome(FMD)),
        valid_weights = sum(valid_weight(RAW_WEIGHT)),
        invalid_weights = sum(!valid_weight(RAW_WEIGHT)),
        reporting_states = data.table::uniqueN(STATE)
    ),
    by = YEAR
][order(YEAR)]

annual_audit[
    ,
    missing_fmd_pct := 100 * missing_fmd / respondents
]

save_table(annual_audit, "01_yearly_audit")
print(annual_audit)
```

## 3. Audit missing responses by year and population

This cell checks whether unknown outcomes and selected missing predictors are distributed similarly across study populations. Missing **predictors** will later be retained as explicit `"Missing"` categories for modeling, but missing **FMD outcomes** cannot be classified as `0`.

```{r response-missingness}
# Recognize both true NA and the explicit Missing level used in this project.
is_missing_response <- function(values) {
    missing <- is.na(values)
    labels <- as.character(values)
    missing | (!missing & labels %in% c("", "Missing"))
}

# Count missing outcomes and selected predictor responses by year and cohort.
missingness <- historical[
    ,
    .(
        respondents = .N,
        missing_fmd = sum(!valid_outcome(FMD)),
        missing_income = sum(is_missing_response(INCOME_BAND)),
        missing_general_health = sum(is_missing_response(GENHLTH_CLEAN)),
        missing_physical_days = sum(is_missing_response(PHYSHLTH_DAYS))
    ),
    by = .(YEAR, cohort)
][order(YEAR, cohort)]

missingness[
    ,
    missing_fmd_pct := 100 * missing_fmd / respondents
]

save_table(missingness, "01_missingness_by_year_and_group")
print(missingness)
```

## 4. Examine annual survey-weight distributions

This measures how unequally the original **annual** weights are distributed. The Kish effective sample size is a *weight-only diagnostic*; it is **not** a full design-based effective sample size and should not be used as the denominator of a confidence interval.

```{r annual-weights}
# Summarize respondent weights before outcome-based exclusions.
weight_audit <- historical[
    valid_weight(RAW_WEIGHT),
    .(
        respondents = .N,
        min_weight = min(RAW_WEIGHT),
        median_weight = median(RAW_WEIGHT),
        mean_weight = mean(RAW_WEIGHT),
        max_weight = max(RAW_WEIGHT),
        effective_n = sum(RAW_WEIGHT)^2 / sum(RAW_WEIGHT^2)
    ),
    by = YEAR
][order(YEAR)]

weight_audit[
    ,
    effective_n_pct := 100 * effective_n / respondents
]

save_table(weight_audit, "01_annual_weight_audit")
print(weight_audit)
```

## 5. Compare weight-only effective sample sizes across populations

This cell uses respondents with a valid FMD outcome to show how much weight inequality reduces the information available within each comparison group. It helps explain why AI/AN annual intervals may be wider despite thousands of survey responses.

```{r group-weights}
# Keep outcome-valid respondents in the two prespecified populations.
valid_groups <- historical[
    valid_outcome(FMD) &
        valid_weight(RAW_WEIGHT) &
        cohort %in% primary_groups
]

# Retain the counts required for prevalence-table interpretation.
group_weight_audit <- valid_groups[
    ,
    .(
        n = .N,
        median_weight = median(RAW_WEIGHT),
        max_weight = max(RAW_WEIGHT),
        effective_n = sum(RAW_WEIGHT)^2 / sum(RAW_WEIGHT^2)
    ),
    by = .(YEAR, cohort)
][order(YEAR, cohort)]

group_weight_audit[
    ,
    effective_n_pct := 100 * effective_n / n
]

save_table(group_weight_audit, "01_group_weight_audit")
print(group_weight_audit)
```

## 6. Verify the structure of the survey-design identifiers

This cell checks the yearly sampling-stratum and PSU identifiers and verifies whether each `STRAT`–`PSU` combination is unique within its year. The revised variance calculation below uses **one public-use record per sampling unit** (`ids = ~1`), matching the 2024 structure you observed. If another year has repeated within-stratum PSU pairs, the notebook stops rather than silently imposing the wrong design.

**This is a structural check only:** You must still verify the `RAW_WEIGHT`, `STRAT`, and `PSU` mappings against your CDC extraction code. One-respondent strata also require an explicit variance-adjustment rule.

```{r survey-identifier-audit}
# Count sampling identifiers within each survey year.
design_audit <- historical[
    ,
    {
        unique_pairs <- data.table::uniqueN(.SD, by = c("STRAT", "PSU"))

        .(
            respondents = .N,
            unique_strata = data.table::uniqueN(STRAT),
            unique_psu_values = data.table::uniqueN(PSU),
            unique_stratum_psu_pairs = unique_pairs,
            duplicated_stratum_psu_pairs = .N - unique_pairs,
            missing_strata = sum(is.na(STRAT)),
            missing_psus = sum(is.na(PSU))
        )
    },
    by = YEAR,
    .SDcols = c("STRAT", "PSU")
][order(YEAR)]

save_table(design_audit, "01_survey_identifier_audit")
print(design_audit)

# Halt if any year violates the one-record-per-pair assumption.
if (any(design_audit$duplicated_stratum_psu_pairs > 0)) {
    stop("Repeated stratum-PSU pairs found: verify the design before computing CIs.")
}

if (any(design_audit$missing_strata > 0 | design_audit$missing_psus > 0)) {
    stop("Missing design identifiers found: resolve before computing CIs.")
}
```

## 7. Detail the 2024 design diagnostic

This replicates the 2024 check we discussed, including the number of strata containing only one respondent. The number of singleton strata matters because the `survey` package needs a documented method for estimating their variance contribution.

```{r design-2024-details}
# Count respondents per stratum and public-use PSU in 2024.
records_2024 <- historical[YEAR == 2024]
psu_pairs_2024 <- records_2024[
    ,
    .(respondents = .N),
    by = .(STRAT, PSU)
]

strata_2024 <- psu_pairs_2024[
    ,
    .(psus_in_stratum = .N),
    by = STRAT
]

design_summary_2024 <- data.table::data.table(
    respondents = nrow(records_2024),
    distinct_psu_values = data.table::uniqueN(records_2024$PSU),
    distinct_stratum_psu_pairs = nrow(psu_pairs_2024),
    multi_respondent_units = sum(psu_pairs_2024$respondents > 1),
    singleton_strata = sum(strata_2024$psus_in_stratum == 1)
)

save_table(design_summary_2024, "01_survey_design_2024")
print(design_summary_2024)
```

## 8. Estimate annual FMD prevalence and its 95% confidence intervals

This is the **main descriptive analysis**. For each year from 2014 to 2024, the code first constructs a stratified survey design using **all records with usable annual weights**. Only *after* constructing the design does it subset to the two populations. Unknown mental-health outcomes are kept as `NA` and excluded by `na.rm = TRUE` when estimating prevalence.

Annual point estimates use the year-specific `RAW_WEIGHT`, not a pooled multiyear weight. Standard errors and intervals account for the specified stratification and weights. The lonely-PSU adjustment is an approximation; results depend on correct original CDC variable mappings and preprocessing exclusions.

```{r survey-prevalence-by-year}
# Apply an explicit adjustment for strata or domains with one PSU.
options(
    survey.lonely.psu = "adjust",
    survey.adjust.domain.lonely = TRUE
)

# Work one year at a time to avoid constructing a giant pooled survey object.
prevalence_rows <- vector("list", length = 11L)
gap_rows <- vector("list", length = 11L)
analysis_years <- 2014:2024

for (year_index in seq_along(analysis_years)) {
    year <- analysis_years[year_index]
    cat("[SURVEY] Estimating", year, "\n")

    # Keep all source records with valid annual weights for the design.
    data_year <- data.table::copy(
        historical[YEAR == year & valid_weight(RAW_WEIGHT)]
    )

    # Preserve unknown FMD outcomes as missing, never as a negative response.
    data_year[
        ,
        fmd_value := ifelse(valid_outcome(FMD), as.numeric(FMD), NA_real_)
    ]

    # Construct the full annual design before subgroup restriction.
    annual_design <- survey::svydesign(
        ids = ~1,
        strata = ~STRAT,
        weights = ~RAW_WEIGHT,
        data = as.data.frame(data_year)
    )

    group_design <- subset(
        annual_design,
        cohort %in% primary_groups
    )

    # Estimate each group's prevalence and their joint covariance matrix.
    group_estimates <- survey::svyby(
        ~fmd_value,
        ~cohort,
        design = group_design,
        FUN = survey::svymean,
        na.rm = TRUE,
        vartype = "se",
        covmat = TRUE
    )

    # Match the named cohorts; never assume the result's row ordering.
    observed_groups <- as.character(group_estimates$cohort)
    group_indices <- match(primary_groups, observed_groups)

    if (anyNA(group_indices)) {
        stop("Missing one of the two study groups in survey year ", year)
    }

    estimates <- as.numeric(stats::coef(group_estimates))[group_indices]
    covariance <- as.matrix(stats::vcov(group_estimates))[
        group_indices,
        group_indices,
        drop = FALSE
    ]

    standard_errors <- sqrt(diag(covariance))
    degrees_of_freedom <- survey::degf(group_design)
    critical_value <- stats::qt(0.975, df = degrees_of_freedom)

    # Group-specific annual prevalence and design-based confidence intervals.
    prevalence_rows[[year_index]] <- data.table::data.table(
        YEAR = year,
        cohort = primary_groups,
        observed_fmd = estimates,
        se = standard_errors,
        ci_l = estimates - critical_value * standard_errors,
        ci_u = estimates + critical_value * standard_errors,
        degrees_of_freedom = degrees_of_freedom
    )

    # Directly estimate the AI/AN minus comparison prevalence difference.
    contrast <- c(1, -1)
    difference <- sum(contrast * estimates)
    difference_se <- sqrt(
        as.numeric(t(contrast) %*% covariance %*% contrast)
    )

    gap_rows[[year_index]] <- data.table::data.table(
        YEAR = year,
        gap_pp = 100 * difference,
        se_pp = 100 * difference_se,
        ci_l_pp = 100 * (difference - critical_value * difference_se),
        ci_u_pp = 100 * (difference + critical_value * difference_se),
        degrees_of_freedom = degrees_of_freedom
    )

    # Release large design objects before processing the next survey year.
    rm(data_year, annual_design, group_design, group_estimates)
}

annual_prevalence <- data.table::rbindlist(prevalence_rows)
annual_gap <- data.table::rbindlist(gap_rows)

# Join respondent counts and weight-only effective n to each group estimate.
annual_prevalence <- merge(
    annual_prevalence,
    group_weight_audit[, .(YEAR, cohort, n, effective_n, effective_n_pct)],
    by = c("YEAR", "cohort"),
    all.x = TRUE,
    sort = FALSE
)

data.table::setorder(annual_prevalence, YEAR, cohort)
data.table::setorder(annual_gap, YEAR)

# Store the exact values that appear in the two figures.
save_table(annual_prevalence, "01_annual_fmd_prevalence")
save_table(annual_gap, "01_annual_fmd_gap")

print(annual_prevalence)
print(annual_gap)
```

## 9. Figure 1 — Annual FMD prevalence with confidence intervals

**What it measures:** the estimated proportion reporting frequent mental distress in each year, separately for the two populations. The shaded ribbons are **95% design-based confidence intervals**, not individual prediction intervals. A higher line does not reveal what caused the difference.

```{r annual-prevalence-figure, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}
# Plot annual estimates and group-specific uncertainty ribbons.
prevalence_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    annual_prevalence,
    ggplot2::aes(
        x = YEAR,
        y = observed_fmd,
        color = cohort,
        group = cohort
    )
) +
    ggplot2::geom_ribbon(
        ggplot2::aes(ymin = ci_l, ymax = ci_u, fill = cohort),
        alpha = 0.16,
        color = NA
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.5) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2014:2024) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
        breaks = seq(0, 0.30, by = 0.05),
        labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
        expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.03))
    ) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
        ylim = c(0, max(annual_prevalence$ci_u, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.06)
    ) +
    atg_scale_color_groups() +
    atg_scale_fill_groups() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Frequent mental distress, 2014–2024",
        subtitle = "Survey-weighted annual prevalence with 95% confidence intervals",
        x = "BRFSS survey year",
        y = "Adults reporting frequent mental distress",
        color = "Population",
        fill = "Population",
        caption = paste(
            "FMD = 14+ mentally unhealthy days in the past 30 days.",
            "Annual cross-sectional estimates; reporting states vary by year.",
            "Intervals depend on verified BRFSS design-variable mappings."
        )
    )

# Print the chart inside this notebook and save it with the current run suffix.
show_and_save(prevalence_plot, "01_annual_fmd_prevalence", 11, 6)
```

## 10. Figure 2 — Annual AI/AN prevalence difference with confidence intervals

**What it measures:** the percentage-point difference between AI/AN-alone and other single-race annual FMD prevalence. Positive values mean higher estimated prevalence among AI/AN-alone adults; an interval spanning zero indicates that the difference is not distinguishable from zero at the 95% confidence level under the specified design. This is a *difference of prevalence*, **not** a difference in model accuracy.

```{r annual-gap-figure, fig.width=11, fig.height=5}
# Plot the annual group contrast with its directly calculated standard error.
gap_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    annual_gap,
    ggplot2::aes(x = YEAR, y = gap_pp)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(
        yintercept = 0,
        linetype = "dashed",
        color = atg_palette[["gold"]],
        linewidth = 0.6
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_errorbar(
        ggplot2::aes(ymin = ci_l_pp, ymax = ci_u_pp),
        width = 0.18,
        linewidth = 0.65,
        color = atg_palette[["turquoise"]]
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(color = atg_palette[["turquoise"]], linewidth = 1.1) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(color = atg_palette[["turquoise"]], size = 2.5) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2014:2024) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
        labels = function(values) paste0(round(values, 1), " pp")
    ) +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "AI/AN versus comparison prevalence gap, 2014–2024",
        subtitle = "AI/AN alone minus other identified single-race adults",
        x = "BRFSS survey year",
        y = "Difference in prevalence (percentage points)",
        caption = paste(
            "Error bars show 95% survey-design confidence intervals",
            "for the difference, not separate group intervals.",
            "The zero line means no difference."
        )
    )

# Show the plot inline and save a numbered copy with the current run.
show_and_save(gap_plot, "01_annual_fmd_gap", 11, 5)
```

## 11. Check the 2024 result and record interpretation

Highlights the same 2024 calculation. It should reproduce approximately **21.35%** AI/AN prevalence, **15.19%** comparison prevalence, and **+6.16 percentage points** with a **95% CI around +4.03 to +8.30 points**, assuming the data and design settings are unchanged. The check prints the numbers from this run rather than inserting hard-coded results into any chart.

```{r check-2024}
# Display 2024 subgroup estimates and the direct between-group contrast.
comparison_2024 <- annual_prevalence[
    YEAR == 2024,
    .(
        cohort,
        respondents = n,
        prevalence_pct = round(100 * observed_fmd, 2),
        ci_lower_pct = round(100 * ci_l, 2),
        ci_upper_pct = round(100 * ci_u, 2),
        effective_n = round(effective_n)
    )
]

gap_2024 <- annual_gap[
    YEAR == 2024,
    .(
        difference_pp = round(gap_pp, 2),
        ci_lower_pp = round(ci_l_pp, 2),
        ci_upper_pp = round(ci_u_pp, 2)
    )
]

cat("\n[2024] Population-specific prevalence and 95% intervals\n")
print(comparison_2024)

cat("\n[2024] AI/AN-minus-comparison difference (percentage points)\n")
print(gap_2024)
```

## Interpretation and limitations

- **Population estimates, not predictions:** This notebook describes trends in *reported* FMD, whereas later notebooks test out-of-time predictive classification.
- **Race definition:** "AI/AN alone" excludes multiracial AI/AN respondents; "other identified single-race" is not the whole U.S. population.
- **Missing outcomes:** An unanswered FMD question is not a negative response. Missing responses remain visible in the audit and are omitted from prevalence estimation.
- **Sampling design:** The variance calculations require verified CDC source mappings, accurate retained stratum identifiers, and a documented handling of singleton strata. They do not correct potential nonresponse bias or all differences in survey coverage.
- **Annual geography:** States participating in BRFSS differ across years. These annual estimates do not by themselves establish a causal trend or isolate changes in geographic composition.
- **Effective sample size:** The reported Kish values describe unequal weights, not the complete survey-design effective sample sizes.
- **Run increments:** This notebook inherits the active increment when run from the master and allocates a fresh increment when knitted independently. Existing files are never silently overwritten.
